entity_title: Employer, not worker, obtains the permit
fact_text: For a B/1 expert posting to Israel, the Israeli employer applies to the Population and Immigration Authority for a permit to employ the foreign expert; the worker does not apply for the work permit themselves.
evidence_quote: Israeli employers can use this service to apply for a permit to employ an expert foreign worker in the various regulated industries.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed the relocating professional applies for their own Israeli work visa. Actually the Israeli employer must first obtain the permit to employ the foreign expert from PIBA. Action: have your employer file the PIBA expert-employment permit before you seek the B/1 visa.

entity_title: PIBA expert-permit fee is paid by the employer
fact_text: The PIBA fee for a foreign-expert employment permit is 1,420 NIS for all experts (1,060 NIS for expert chefs), payable by the employer at the end of the online application.
evidence_quote: 1,420 NIS for all experts, excluding chefs

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed the worker pays the visa/permit fee. Actually the employer pays the PIBA expert-permit fee (1,420 NIS; 1,060 NIS for chefs). Action: confirm your employer covers permit costs, not you.

entity_title: Expert track requires expertise unavailable in Israel
fact_text: The foreign-expert ('mumche') track requires a foreign national with a high level of expertise or essential, unique knowledge that is unavailable in Israel, at the sole discretion of the PIBA commissioner.
evidence_quote: a foreign national with a high level of expertise or an essential and unique knowledge for the service provided by the employer and unavailable in Israel

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed any skilled professional qualifies for the expert permit. Actually the expert track requires knowledge 'unavailable in Israel'. Action: document why the role cannot be filled by the local labour market.

entity_title: Expert wages must be at least double the average wage
fact_text: To be approved on 'expert wages', the foreign expert's gross monthly base pay must be at least double the average gross wage of a salaried employee as published by the National Insurance Institute.
evidence_quote: the Foreign Expert shall be paid a gross monthly base wages that is not less than double the average gross wages of a salaried employee

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed a competitive market salary is enough. Actually the expert permit requires gross pay of at least twice the national average wage published by the NII. Action: budget the salary at 2x or more of the NII average wage before applying.

entity_title: First expert permit is capped at 1-2 years
fact_text: A first-time expert-wages permit is valid for a maximum of two years for professions requiring higher academic education, and a maximum of one year (or less) for professions that do not; it is then subject to renewal.
evidence_quote: expert wages” in professions that require higher academic education shall be valid for a maximum period of two years

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed a work visa is granted for the whole assignment up front. Actually the first expert permit is capped at two years (academic roles) or one year (others) and must be renewed. Action: plan renewal timing into the assignment.

entity_title: Work is tied to the sponsoring employer and field
fact_text: The B/1 expert permit ties the worker to the specific sponsoring employer and field; working for another employer in the field of expertise requires prior written authorization from the Authority.
evidence_quote: he may not work for another employer in the field of expertise for which he was invited to work in Israel without written authorization from the Authority

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed a work visa lets you change jobs freely. Actually the B/1 expert permit binds you to the sponsoring employer; changing employer or field needs prior written PIBA authorization. Action: never start with a new employer before authorization is granted.

entity_title: Stay is for a limited period; leave when employment ends
fact_text: The foreign expert is admitted for a limited period equal to the employer's permit and must leave Israel immediately when the employment ends.
evidence_quote: he is to arrive in Israel for a limited period, which is the period specified in the employment permit issued to the Applicant, that he is required to leave Israel immediately

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed you can stay in Israel to job-hunt after the assignment ends. Actually the permit is for a limited period and you must leave immediately when employment ends. Action: arrange a transfer or departure before the permit lapses.

entity_title: Employer must provide private medical insurance
fact_text: The employer is legally obligated to provide the foreign expert with medical insurance under section 1d of the Foreign Workers Law, at the employer's expense; foreign workers are not in the resident public-health system.
evidence_quote: the obligation to provide the Foreign Expert with medical insurance in accordance with section 1d of the Foreign Workers Law, at the expense of the employer

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed you join the public HMO (Kupat Holim) system like Israeli residents. Actually foreign workers are outside national health insurance and the employer must arrange private medical insurance at its expense. Action: confirm your employer's private health policy is active on arrival.

fact_text: The employer is obligated to provide the foreign expert with adequate accommodation (and medical insurance) under section 1d of the Foreign Workers Law, at the employer's expense.
evidence_quote: the obligation to provide the Foreign Expert with adequate accommodation and medical insurance in accordance with section 1d of the Foreign Workers Law, at the expense of the employer

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed housing is entirely the worker's own responsibility. Actually the employer has a statutory duty to provide adequate accommodation (and medical insurance) at its expense. Action: clarify the accommodation arrangement and any capped rent deduction in your contract.

entity_title: Residency turns on the 'center of life' test
fact_text: Whether a person is an Israeli resident (which determines National Insurance status, and mirrors the income-tax residency concept) is decided by the 'center of life' test, not citizenship or a simple day-count.
evidence_quote: A person whose life is centered in Israel. Criteria for determining this include: Israel is your permanent place of residence, where your family resides, where your children go to school

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed residency is set by citizenship or a fixed number of days. Actually Israeli residency turns on your 'center of life' (home, family, children's schooling, main work). Action: expect to be treated as a non-resident foreign worker unless your center of life shifts to Israel.

entity_title: Employer pays National Insurance for the foreign worker
fact_text: An employer of someone who is not an Israeli resident is the employer of a foreign worker and must file a report and pay National Insurance contributions for that worker.
evidence_quote: you are considered the employer of a foreign worker and you must file a report on that worker and pay national insurance contributions for him or her

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed non-residents are outside the National Insurance system entirely. Actually the employer must report and pay National Insurance contributions even for a non-resident foreign worker. Action: check your payslip reflects NII deductions/contributions.

entity_title: Foreign workers are insured for work injury
fact_text: Even as a non-resident, a foreign worker is insured against work injury: a foreign worker recognized as a work-injury victim is entitled by law to medical care for the recognized injury.
evidence_quote: A foreign worker recognized as victim of work injury will be eligible by law for medical care related to the recognized injury

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed foreign workers get no National Insurance benefits at all. Actually a foreign worker is insured for work injury and is entitled by law to medical care for a recognized injury. Action: report any workplace injury to the NII to claim work-injury rights.
